claims.text: Local short-range chemical ordering at Al- and Ni-rich sites governs fcc/B2 phase stability in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys.
The relevant baseline cast Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy has a stable dual-phase fcc + B2 microstructure after standard solutionizing and quenching.
Short-range ordering coherently pins fcc/B2 phase boundaries.
The short-range-order-stabilized dual-phase structure enhances high-temperature strength.
The short-range-order-stabilized dual-phase structure enhances corrosion or oxidation resistance.
The short-range-order-stabilized dual-phase structure enhances radiation tolerance.
The short-range-order-stabilized dual-phase structure enhances cryogenic toughness or ductility.
Heat-treatment temperature and time can be used to vary short-range order in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni.
Changing Al content can alter chemical ordering or clustering in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni.
Small changes in Ni content can systematically vary short-range order in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni.
The degree of short-range order influences nucleation of B2 domains within an fcc matrix.
The degree of short-range order controls the spatial distribution of B2 domains within an fcc matrix.
Enhanced ordering at Al- and Ni-rich sites stabilizes B2 domains.
Increasing short-range order increases hardness or strength.
Increasing short-range order produces stronger and more chemically stable fcc/B2 interfaces.
Enhanced short-range order prevents intergranular deterioration during irradiation.
Enhanced short-range order prevents low-temperature embrittlement.
Samples with reduced local ordering have a stronger tendency toward a single-phase structure.
Extreme Al content can cause the stabilizing effect of short-range order to fade.
Temperatures beyond a critical ordering range cause phase coarsening and reduced property benefits.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state calls the baseline a dual-phase fcc + B2 alloy, whereas the baseline field says minimally ordered samples are expected to show stronger single-phase tendencies, leaving the baseline phase state inconsistent.

The intervention proposes adding Al or Ni while maintaining overall alloy stoichiometry. An elemental addition changes the stoichiometric ratios unless a compensating reduction of other elements is specified.
